subject: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@atlas-systems.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request

Hi team,

Atlas is starting the final integration sprint for the personalization pilot and has asked for a short-term carve (2–3 weeks) from our US GPU pool to avoid noisy preemption during their end-to-end tests. They’re requesting roughly 12 A100-equivalent slots, primarily daytime hours, with autoscale relaxed during their test window.

Before we commit, I want to ensure we have a quick operational safety matrix that:
- Defines the carve timeframe and hours-of-day windows
- Documents fallback models (smaller variants) and automatic routing policies
- Lists the autoscaling exceptions we’d tolerate (queue depth thresholds, burst-to-reserve rules)

Marcus / Kimberly / Laura — can we align on the minimal gating criteria (SLO impact threshold, preemption budget, owner escalation) so I can sign off with the Atlas SREs this afternoon? I’ve copied their infra alias so we don’t go back-and-forth on basic details.

Thanks,
Jonas

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@atlas-systems.com
Date: 2026-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request

Thanks Jonas — quick replies inline below and I uploaded a draft matrix to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBzQ-safety-matrix (file: safety_matrix_v1.xlsx).

- Timeframe: Tentative 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-21 (client prefers weekdays, daytime peak 9a–6p PT). We should confirm exact window after we set autoscale rules.
- Fallback models: mark Atlas model as primary; fallback to q4-7 quantized variants (same family) with routing policy that falls back after 300ms extra latency or 5% regression in key eval prompts.
- Autoscaling exceptions: propose a temporary override to burst-to-reserve threshold (allow 80% burst usage before reserve pulls) and increase per-request concurrency cap for the pilot tenant to 12, instead of the usual 8.

Operational asks for infra:
- Marcus, can you confirm if we can support the cap bump without violating existing headroom SLOs?
- Laura, product needs a go/no-go by EOD Friday so we can lock the pilot launch date.

If infra can’t support the 12-slot daytime carve, what minimum number would be acceptable for Atlas to still run their long tails reliably (they asked if 6 would be workable)?

-kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@atlas-systems.com
Date: 2026-09-30T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request

Thanks — quick technical read: I attached a short allocation proposal (allocation_proposal.pdf) that models three options (12/day carve, 8/day carve, 6/day carve) and the expected latency/regression impact under our current autoscaler. Key notes:

- 12-slot carve (preferred by Atlas): would increase preemption pressure on other pilot slices by ~10% during daytime but keeps Atlas within their performance SLO. We can mitigate with a soft-preempt policy that first shifts noncritical batch jobs.
- 8-slot carve (compromise): marginally increases tail latency (p50 unaffected, p95 +12–18%), still acceptable for non-critical pilots.
- 6-slot carve (minimum): likely causes repeated model fallbacks after sustained traffic spikes — Atlas might need to accept higher fallback rate.

Autoscale exception mechanics I can implement:
- A temporary rule set that relaxes the burst-to-reserve threshold and raises per-tenant concurrency caps. This is a config flag and a short runbook for ops to revert.
- I’ll need an explicit approval window and owner (on-call or Marcus team) to act if the carve causes system-wide SLO slips.

Action items for me: I’ll drop the allocation_proposal.pdf into the Drive folder and add a simple runbook.

Attachments: allocation_proposal.pdf (stub)

—Marcus
Senior Infra PM
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request

Appreciate the fast follow. Product side: Atlas’ integration is time-boxed — hitting the 10/21 date matters for their contract milestone. If the infra tradeoff is limited to a small p95 hit for other pilots for 2–3 weeks, product can accept that with the following conditions:

1) We require a rollback trigger: any system-wide increase in p95 above 20% for more than 3 consecutive hours triggers immediate revert.
2) A single named owner for the carve window (on-call name/email) and a Slack channel for fast comms.
3) IR checklist: who escalates to leadership if rollback happens.

Kimberly — if infra can provide the owner and the runbook by EOD Wednesday (10/06), product will greenlight the 12-slot carve. If not, we default to the 8-slot compromise.

-LaurA
Product Lead, Routing & Performance
Redwood Inference

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@atlas-systems.com, sre@cloudvendor.com
Date: 2026-10-02T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Safety matrix + short-term GPU allocation request

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps:

- Decision: Tentatively greenlight 12-slot daytime carve for 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-21, conditional on two items below.
- Infra (Marcus): please publish the runbook and config flags (INF-3421) and assign an on-call owner for the carve window by 2026-10-06 17:00 PT. Confirm the rollback automation (p95 trigger) is in place.
- Product (Laura / Kimberly): confirm acceptance of fallback routing thresholds and sign off on the SLA exception.
- External: Atlas infra-ops, please confirm the exact hours you require (we suggested 9a–6p PT) and sign the mutual action plan in the Drive folder.

Attachments referenced: safety_matrix_v1.xlsx, allocation_proposal.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBzQ-safety-matrix
Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-3421

I’ll coordinate a 30-minute sync tomorrow if anyone prefers a quick call rather than email.

Jonas
